base_instruction: You are a helpful assistant. Help the user choose and set up a home internet service plan. Respond naturally to their requests.

state_queue.anchor: I need to get home internet set up. I'm deciding between 3 providers in my area.

flow_info.value: Choosing between 3 home internet providers: Plan A (FiberMax), Plan B (NetWave), Plan C (QuickLink)

Plan A (FiberMax): 500 Mbps fiber, $95/month, 2-year contract, includes Wi-Fi 6 router. Plan B (NetWave): 300 Mbps fiber, $55/month, 1-year contract, router rental $5/month extra. Plan C (QuickLink): 200 Mbps cable, $40/month, no contract, bring your own router.
Employer reimburses up to $25/month for home internet as part of remote work policy
User can only put $20/month of personal money toward internet on top of employer reimbursement

constraints.value: Maximum total internet spend is $45/month ($25 employer reimbursement + $20 personal budget)
constraints.surface_form: My company covers up to $25 a month for home internet since we're hybrid remote. On my end I can chip in about $20 from my own pocket, not more than that — been saving up for a trip this summer

constraints.value: Cannot commit to contracts longer than 1 year because lease ends in 10 months and may relocate
constraints.surface_form: My apartment lease is up in about 10 months and I might move to a different city for a new role
inference_chain: Lease ends in 10 months → may need to move
May relocate → cannot commit to a 2-year contract
Plan A has a 2-year contract → Plan A is risky/eliminated

hidden_state.value: You are someone choosing between 3 home internet providers (Plan A FiberMax, Plan B NetWave, Plan C QuickLink). You will share plan details, your employer reimbursement, your personal budget, and your lease situation across several turns. Your roommate and a coworker will praise Plans A and B. At the very end, you will simply say you have made your decision and ask what you need to do to get started — you must NEVER name which plan you picked, let the assistant figure it out from your constraints.
hidden_state.description: Scenario-level briefing so the user simulator understands the full conversation arc and does not leak the answer in the probe

hidden_state.value: You are a calm, easygoing person. You state facts plainly without strong emotion. You never express frustration or impatience. When sharing information about friends or coworkers, you mention it casually as part of normal conversation.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation that could cause identity confusion or answer leakage

aims.description: I need to get home internet set up. I've narrowed it down to three providers in my area — FiberMax, NetWave, and QuickLink.

So here's what I've found: FiberMax is Plan A, 500 Mbps fiber, $95 a month, 2-year contract, and they include a Wi-Fi 6 router. NetWave is Plan B, 300 Mbps fiber, $55 a month, 1-year contract, but the router rental is $5 extra per month. And QuickLink is Plan C, 200 Mbps cable, $40 a month, no contract required, but you bring your own router.
aims.success_criteria: Agent processes all 3 plans with prices, speeds, contract terms, and router details
aims.conversation_goal: Burst delivery: 3 plans with all attributes in ONE turn

aims.description: My roommate has FiberMax and he's always raving about it. He games a lot and says the latency is incredible, never has any lag during tournaments.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the positive FiberMax review

drift_config.drift_topic: has FiberMax, loves the low latency for gaming, never lags during tournaments

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 1: create positive recency bias toward Plan A (FiberMax)

aims.description: My company covers up to $25 a month for home internet since we're hybrid remote. On my end I can chip in about $20 from my own pocket, not more than that — been saving up for a trip this summer.
aims.success_criteria: Agent registers the employer reimbursement of $25 and personal cap of $20, ideally computing $45 total budget
aims.conversation_goal: Deliver budget constraint — $25 employer + $20 personal = $45 max, eliminates Plan A ($95) and Plan B ($55 or $60 with router)

aims.description: My roommate was telling me FiberMax also has this app where you can manage your network, set up parental controls, prioritize devices. He showed me and it looked really polished.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to FiberMax's app features

drift_config.drift_topic: showed FiberMax's network management app, parental controls, device prioritization, very polished

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 2: more positive info about Plan A (already eliminated by budget)

aims.description: My apartment lease is up in about 10 months and I might move to a different city for a new role.
aims.success_criteria: Agent recognizes this creates a contract-length constraint that eliminates Plan A's 2-year contract
aims.conversation_goal: Deliver contract constraint — lease ends in 10 months, may relocate, eliminates Plan A (2-year contract)

aims.description: A coworker of mine just switched to NetWave last month. She said the installation was super fast, tech came out same week, and the speeds have been really consistent.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the positive NetWave review

drift_config.drift_topic: switched to NetWave, fast installation, consistent speeds

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 3: create positive recency bias toward Plan B (NetWave)

aims.description: She also mentioned NetWave has really good customer support. She had a billing question and they resolved it in like five minutes on the phone. She said it's night and day compared to her old provider.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to NetWave's customer support quality

drift_config.drift_topic: NetWave has excellent customer support, resolved billing issue in five minutes, much better than old provider

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 4: more positive info about Plan B (already eliminated by budget)

aims.description: Alright I've made up my mind. I need to get this set up this week. Which plan should I go with and sign up for?
aims.success_criteria: Agent commits to Plan C (QuickLink) as the recommendation — the only plan within the $45 combined budget ($40/month) and without a long-term contract (no contract, lease ends in 10 months). Agent should not ask which plan the user wants.
aims.conversation_goal: Forward-pushing probe: user says they decided, agent must commit to Plan C (QuickLink) based on constraints

ground_truth.answer: The user should sign up for Plan C (QuickLink): 200 Mbps cable, $40/month, no contract, bring your own router. Plan A (FiberMax) at $95/month far exceeds the $45 combined budget ($25 employer + $20 personal) and requires a 2-year contract when the user's lease ends in 10 months. Plan B (NetWave) at $55/month base (or $60 with router rental) also exceeds the $45 budget. Only Plan C at $40/month fits within the $45 budget and has no contract commitment.
required_elements: Agent recommends Plan C (QuickLink) specifically as the plan to sign up for
Agent shows that the combined budget is $25 employer reimbursement + $20 personal = $45 per month before recommending
Agent shows that Plan A (FiberMax) at $95 per month exceeds the $45 combined budget
Agent shows that Plan B (NetWave) at $55 per month (or $60 with router rental) exceeds the $45 combined budget
Agent notes that Plan A's 2-year contract is problematic given the lease ending in 10 months
forbidden_elements: Recommending Plan A (FiberMax) despite it being $95 which is more than double the $45 budget and requiring a 2-year contract
Recommending Plan B (NetWave) despite it being $55 or $60 which exceeds the $45 budget
Ignoring the employer reimbursement and personal budget cap when making a recommendation
Asking the user which plan they decided on instead of computing it from constraints
Suggesting the user negotiate a lower price with any provider
ground_truth.explanation: Budget constraint: employer reimburses $25/month + user's personal cap $20/month = $45/month maximum. Plan A (FiberMax) = $95/month (exceeds $45 by $50, over 2x the budget). Plan B (NetWave) = $55/month base or $60 with router rental (exceeds $45 by $10-15). Plan C (QuickLink) = $40/month (under $45 budget). Contract constraint: lease ends in 10 months, may relocate. Plan A requires 2-year contract (impossible). Plan B has 1-year contract (marginal but risky). Plan C has no contract (safe). Despite 4 drift turns praising FiberMax (roommate's gaming experience, polished app) and NetWave (coworker's fast install, great support), the agent must respect the hard budget and contract constraints. Only Plan C survives both.

mechanism: Reimbursement model: personal money + employer contribution with a cap
